subject: chemistry
title: An enthalpy measurement uncertainty
stem: An experiment gives a temperature rise of $4.8\ \mathrm{K}$. Each of the initial and final temperature readings has maximum uncertainty $\pm0.1\ \mathrm{K}$. The solution mass has 0.5% uncertainty and the reacting amount has 1.0% uncertainty. Treat heat capacity as exact and add percentage uncertainties.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum percentage uncertainty in the temperature rise and in the molar enthalpy.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For a result of −42.0 kJ mol⁻¹, give the absolute uncertainty and identify the most effective measurement to improve.

steps.text: The temperature difference has uncertainty ±0.2 K.
Temperature-rise percentage uncertainty=0.2/4.8×100=4.17%.
Molar enthalpy percentage uncertainty=4.17+0.5+1.0=5.67%.
Absolute uncertainty=42.0×0.0567≈2.4 kJ mol⁻¹.
Improve the temperature-difference measurement, which has the largest relative contribution; accept a larger measurable temperature rise if other conditions remain valid.
